Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1979. Behind the Goalkeeping Crisis Rocking West Ham

While Mads Hermansen’s recent performances have come under scrutiny and Finlay Herrick has found the transition challenging, culminating in his role in Portsmouth’s winning goal on Tuesday night, I still believe Herrick has the attributes to succeed. His potential is clear, but it requires time, guidance and development.

Meanwhile, supporters continue to ask why Alphonse Areola has not been available for first-team selection.

Let’s start with the facts. Alphonse Areola is no messiah. Last season, the French goalkeeper conceded 37 goals in 20 Premier League appearances, made 77 saves and failed to keep a single clean sheet. At the start of this season, Areola was informed that he was no longer Nuno’s first-choice goalkeeper. Despite having just one year remaining on his contract and reportedly taking a 50 per cent reduction in salary, now believed to be around £60,000 per week, no offers materialised. That still makes him one of the highest-paid goalkeepers in the Championship.

This season, he has been named on the bench nine times in 17 matches. However, questions remain over his fitness. Earlier in the campaign, he was sidelined with an unspecified injury despite being photographed attending a tennis tournament. He then reportedly suffered another setback during the warm-up ahead of the Blackburn Rovers match on 7 November, although the club has yet to officially disclose the nature of the injury.

Scott Parker has offered little clarity, saying only that “the club was struggling a bit with Alphonse” and describing his availability as “touch and go”. Inevitably, conspiracy theories have emerged, with some suggesting the goalkeeper has chosen not to make himself available for selection. However, there is no evidence to substantiate that suggestion, and he attended the Preston game with his family and watched from the stands.

The most likely explanation, as Martin previously outlined, is simply fitness, or a lack of it. For a club with only two recognised senior goalkeepers and one established academy option, the current situation is far from ideal.

While the team’s defensive issues cannot be blamed solely on the goalkeeping department, the number of goals conceded this season has undoubtedly affected results. It is an issue that requires an urgent resolution and one Parker will be acutely aware of.

Another area worth examining is the goalkeeping coaching set-up. Since Xavi Valero’s departure in May 2025, the club has never truly found a settled replacement. Casper Ankergren arrived alongside Linus Kandolin, Rui Barbosa subsequently replaced them and Billy Lepine later stepped into the role. In the space of just 18 months, the club has had four different goalkeeping coaches.

Continuity matters, particularly in such a specialised position, and that level of turnover is far from ideal.

For me, the club already has a ready-made solution in Łukasz Fabiański. His experience, leadership and understanding of the position make him more than qualified to take on such a responsibility.

Whatever the answer, Parker needs to resolve the situation quickly. The clock is ticking.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

I still don’t understand why Areola is unfit. He appears to have done nothing to get injured and I was physio for a major rugby union team for many years. My God, there is a difference between pro rugby players and footballers. If you look at a footballer the wrong way, send for the air-ambulance. Too much money in football.

Let’s set the record straight. It’s not a keeper problem. Its what rubbish we have in front of them The best keepers in the world would struggle with that defence. our club decisions are always barking up the wrong tree. That’s why we are where we are

Look at last season” goalie stats, but from a defender point of view Kilman didnt play in any clean sheet matches whilst Tobido, and a more confident Dinos did.

Yes, poor Herrick made an error last Tuesday, but we didnt lose that match or win the Preston game because of him.

As you say it’s the defence on ftont of the Goalie and the fact we’re hitting the woodwork or shooting/heading straight at the opps goalie

I’m relieved Alvarez is back, because he will at least limit the situation

#1978. Viktor Gyökeres’ Sweden resurgence raises Arsenal questions, but the January exit is far from certain

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Viktor Gyökeres is reminding Arsenal of his prolific goal scoring capabilities.

The striker found the back of the net twice in Sweden’s 3-2 Nations League win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14, both times from the spot to take his total to four in the Nations League this season.

The win also means they have booked their place in League A with one match left to play in the group, and Gyökeres has certainly played his part in this excellent run.

However, the performance will raise questions about his future at the club. The idea that he may be leaving in January is a possibility that needs to be looked at.

There is a stark difference between his international and club form.

Gyökeres has only played 181 minutes in seven Premier League games this season, starting just once as Kai Havertz has usually been preferred in central areas.

However, he has had more opportunities to play in European competition. Gyökeres has started three of Arsenal’s four matches in the Champions League, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

Gyökeres is not totally out of Arteta’s plans, but he will not play much domestically.

He has been in fine form internationally recently. Sweden are building their attack around his movement and penalty area presence, meaning he will have chances to regularly perform.

However, just because he is doing well internationally does not mean he will start regularly for the club. Arteta has other attacking options and tactics to consider.

There have been suggestions surrounding Gyökeres’ future, with reports that Arsenal may look to add more attacking flair to their squad.

AC Milan and Juventus have also been linked, but there is no agreement or suggestion that either club is looking to make a January move for the forward.

Gyökeres has opened up about the speculation.

In an interview with Swedish media outlet Fotbollskanalen during the international break, he stated that he would like to stay at the club. The player also denied any issues with his relationship with Arteta, stating that they have good communication.

However, the player may not stay forever, as he has not played much in the Premier League so far. If this continues, and Arsenal sign another forward, it could cause an issue.

For now, though, there is little evidence that Gyökeres is trying to leave the club.

He’ll be looking to get regular game time at 28 after finding his scoring touch with Sweden. Arsenal will also need to work out how to use him best as a goalscoring striker.

But for now the January speculation seems a little early. He has stated he wants to stay at Arsenal, and the next few weeks may prove to be more important.

#1977. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#1974. David Raya and Jurrien Timber deals show Arsenal are serious about protecting their title-winning core

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are continuing their excellent work in retaining their key players as David Raya and Jurrien Timber have both been approached about new contracts.

This comes after Declan Rice signed a five-year contract extension. The midfielder will now stay at the Emirates until 2031, but Mikel Arteta is now close to locking down more defenders in his squad.

Timber has reportedly agreed better terms, and Raya is also on the verge of a new deal. Although both deals are yet to be officially announced, it shows how important Arsenal are trying to keep them at the top.

The importance of retaining Raya and Timber is evident.

Since arriving at the club from Brentford, Raya has become Arteta’s first choice in goal. He has become an important part of Arsenal’s attacking play due to his distribution, decision-making and game under pressure.

His performances have also earned him honours outside of North London as he was named in the 2026 FIFPRO World 11. Only the second Arsenal player to win the award after Thierry Henry in 2006.

Raya has a contract in place until 2028, although he was given better financial terms last year. However, a new long-term deal will offer more security to one of Arteta’s most trusted players.

Since joining from Ajax in 2023, Timber has become a key part of Arsenal’s backline. Despite injury issues, he has proven to be one of the most dependable defenders in the squad.

He can play as a right back, left back and centre back which provides Arteta with great versatility. He has the physicality and technical ability to help Arsenal at both ends of the pitch.

It has been reported that Timber has agreed to better terms. How long his contract is for is unknown.

There is a pattern beginning to emerge from Arsenal’s recent contract news.

Rice has been signed until 2031. Timber is also expected to sign, committing his peak years to the club. Raya is also expected to sign soon, with talks said to be at an advanced stage.

Arteta recently signed a contract extension until 2030. They aren’t just trying to keep their best players for another year but are looking to create consistency within the squad and management.

This is an issue for any club competing within the domestic and European leagues, as it can cause problems with team cohesion and development due to constant change of key players.

While there is still work to be done, this is positive news for fans.

Signing Raya and Timber will ensure that two key components of Arteta’s backline are safe. It will also show that with Rice’s new contract, they’re looking to build on their recent success and not let their best players near the end of their contracts.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are said to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.

According to reports, negotiations are at an advanced stage between the Ecuadorian and international players. David Raya is also near to signing a new contract as Mikel Arteta looks to retain his key squad members.

However, Hincapié is in a slightly different position compared to his teammates. The 24-year-old only signed a five-year deal permanently in the summer.

Therefore, he could be discussing an increase in his salary rather than an extension. It has not been officially confirmed by either Arsenal or the player.

Arsenal have exercised their option to make Hincapié’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

The defender made 39 appearances in all competitions during his first season in North London, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He has become an important part of Arteta’s defensive options.

His versatility has been an asset to Arsenal. His ability to play as a centre-back or left-back meaning he provides another option to utilise when problems occur with injuries or rotation in defence.

However, Hincapié has been overshadowed by Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori, making it a tough battle for playing time.

In the current campaign, he has played just five games in the league, with all of them coming off the bench. A total of 67 minutes has been played.

Hincapié will not be too concerned by this, as Arsenal have plenty of defensive options, and he provides cover in two positions.

The news that Hincapié is in talks is part of a bigger story around the club trying to keep their best players.

Declan Rice has signed a new five-year deal with Jurrien Timber, signing on improved terms. Raya is also said to be close to signing a new deal.

Arteta has already signed his future to the club until 2030. It is clear that they want to keep the continuity going forward after recent success.

While Hincapié has a contract until next year, renegotiating his deal would show how much Arsenal values him.

They may want to reward their players who have quickly become key members of their squad.

He has no reports of being unhappy and looking to leave the club. It seems he is being rewarded for his contributions to the club and to give him security in the long term.

This is a huge vote of confidence for a player who has only just completed his permanent move this summer.

West Ham United could be forced to wait until the summer if they are to sign River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, according to the latest reports from Argentina. The Hammers have been linked with the highly rated goalkeeper for several weeks, but there appears to be a potential complication regarding the timing of any transfer.

Argentine journalist Juan Cortese has reported that River Plate could agree to sell Beltrán on the condition that he remains with the club until June. As reported this morning by The72, Aston Villa and Fiorentina are also showing interest in the goalkeeper.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

#1969. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

#1967. Parker’s West Ham Snowball Is Already Gathering Pace

Scott Parker was in a particularly festive mood during yesterday’s pre-match press conference ahead of West Ham’s clash with Stoke City on Saturday. The Hammers gaffer trotted out a rather obscure festive analogy about snowballs getting bigger, which is all very well and good.

But if he’s not careful, that little ball of ice could start hurtling down a mountainside and become an avalanche. West Ham are now six games without a victory, and Parker is still awaiting his first win as head coach.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker said: “You have to make sure that little snowball doesn’t become a massive one, and that’s certainly something that’s on my mind.”

One of the things I most liked about Parker’s first couple of interviews was that he didn’t revert to football clichés, and his snowball comparison certainly wasn’t one. But it came amid the usual talk of having to do better and his assertion that we’ll be judged in May.

Probably what concerned me most was that he feels performances have been good. I do believe the Hammers boss is relying heavily on data, and that is something that could be misleading. As the old adage goes, there are lies, damned lies and statistics.

Make no mistake about it, West Ham’s attacking statistics were heavily boosted by a flurry of activity, largely initiated by Tomáš Souček, between the 85th and 90th minutes. By and large, throughout the game at Fratton Park, his team were easily contained.

There are two things Parker must prioritise against Stoke, and it’s going to be a tricky thing to balance because not only must West Ham score first, but they must also ensure that Stoke don’t do the same.

Whoever Parker picks between the sticks will need protecting

Therefore, Parker is going to be caught between a rock and a hard place, wanting to protect whichever nervous goalkeeper is between the sticks whilst trying to ensure West Ham are not left chasing the game from a deficit.

I think it may well mean we’re in for a cagey affair because, whilst the game remains at nil-nil, the worst hasn’t happened. I’m not sure how good that will be for a nervous London Stadium crowd.

Somehow, the Irons boss must get his message across to players who look very short on motivation, which is a concern bearing in mind the manager has only been in the Hammers hot seat for five minutes.

Whether that rousing rallying cry comes in the form of snowballs, chimneys or Santa’s sleigh matters not. Because if Parker doesn’t get a massive improvement from the next few games, he may well find that snowball makes for a very unjolly Christmas.

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he showed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

He claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

This is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

In the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

#1964. “West Ham Captaincy” The Jarrod Bowen Question Nobody Seems To Be Asking

West Ham United captain Jarrod Bowen has dismissed suggestions that the Hammers’ struggles to adapt to Championship football can be used as an excuse for their poor performances. Speaking to talkSPORT last night, Bowen acknowledged that the players simply haven’t been good enough.

The West Ham skipper remains confident that the club can secure promotion back to the Premier League, despite the Hammers having slipped to 13th in the Championship. With second-placed Stoke City visiting the London Stadium on Saturday, Scott Parker is still searching for his first victory as head coach.

When asked about the difficulties of adapting to the Championship, Bowen said: “We can’t lean on that too much, we just have to face up to the facts that we haven’t been good enough.” The Hammers captain also touched upon his playing position during the interview, which was arguably one of the more interesting aspects of the discussion.

I’m pleased that Jarrod Bowen said West Ham haven’t been good enough, but having listened to the talkSPORT interview, I couldn’t help but think that he was trotting out what was expected of him. Understandably, the line of questioning was rather generic.

Personally, I’d have liked to know why Bowen has been stuck out on the wing and been so ineffective for much of the last three games. The Hammers skipper alluded to the fact that he’d not discussed his position with Parker, which I find astounding considering the influence Bowen had in a free role against Cardiff City.

As for the West Ham captaincy, well, the less said about that the better. As Portsmouth went 1-0 up on Tuesday night, a distraught Fin Herrick lay on the ground beating his fist in frustration. He’s a rookie keeper who, in my opinion, had made another mistake and needed guidance.

What did Bowen do? Despite standing next to Herrick, Bowen turned on his heels, dropped his head and walked away, leaving the academy prospect to pick himself up and deal with it. Unacceptable.

Ideally, I’d have preferred a tougher line of questioning, drilling down into the specifics of exactly what is going on with West Ham’s best player. Instead, we got clichéd responses and a pledge that we’ll be involved in the promotion shake-up in May.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

#1959. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1958. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

#1957. West Ham Need A Different Approach As £12m Target Breaks Silence

FC Midtjylland winger Mikel Gogorza has confirmed that West Ham United submitted a concrete transfer offer for him during the summer window. The 20-year-old has also revealed that playing in England remains his dream, despite rejecting the opportunity to join the Hammers.

Speaking to Danish publication Bold following Midtjylland’s 2-0 Conference League victory over Pafos last night, Gogorza explained that the offer arrived whilst he was recovering from a groin injury. According to an English translation of the interview published by Sport Witness, West Ham’s bid was worth approximately £12 million.

Gogorza revealed that both he and his club felt it was important for him to spend another season in Denmark following his injury. With the January transfer window approaching and Scott Parker’s team struggling for attacking inspiration, it’ll be interesting to see whether the Hammers revisit any of their summer transfer targets.

I’d certainly be hoping that West Ham wouldn’t be revisiting their interest in Gogorza, primarily because I don’t believe him to be an upgrade on what we have. He certainly doesn’t appear to be worth a £18 million gamble which is the number currently being quoted.

Look, the jury is still out on Edvin Austbø, who appears to be a promising player. But I’m firmly of the opinion that West Ham do need another winger, ideally one who’s versatile enough to play on both sides.

It would be my preference to have somebody with experience of English football, and I’m intrigued to find out where Nils Koppen has been focusing his interest.

It’s worth remembering that last summer, as Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed at the time, the Hammers hierarchy hired Ben Chorley to assist with identifying Championship-based players.

It is Brighton v Newcastle United up next.

Fabian Hurzeler and his Seagulls taking on Matthias Jaissle’s Magpies.

Brighton v Newcastle United has never featured a Premier League away win for United.

In more than 35 years we have seen only one win for Newcastle at Brighton, a 2-1 Championship victory in the 2016-17 season, featuring that astonishing Mo Diame wonder goal!

Since the 1991-92 season there have only been 12 of these Brighton v Newcastle United matches but it is still not a place high on the expectation list for NUFC fans.

Brighton are second top in the Premier League of course and whilst Newcastle United got that excellent 2-2 draw with Arsenal, Fabian Hurzeler and his team smashed them 3-0 at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton have a Premier League record this season of Played 11 Won 7 Drawn 1 Lost 3.

In all competitions, Brighton’s record is Played 19 Won 12 Drawn 3 Lost 4.

However, the very daunting stats only appear ahead of this Brighton v Newcastle United match when you look at how the Seagulls have got on home and away.

In their 11 away matches in all competitions, Brighton have won 5, drawn 2 and lost 4, scoring 17 goals and conceding 13.

In their 8 home matches (all competitions), Brighton have won 7, drawn 1 and lost none, scoring 27 goals and conceding only 1!!

In over three months, the 1-1 Premier League draw against Leeds on 5 September 2026 is the only time this season that Brighton at home have conceded a goal, failed to win and not managed to score at least two goals on home turf.

The challenge is on for Newcastle United.

#1955. Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction, Odds, H2H and Betting Tips

Ryan Fletcher is a lifelong GTA fan who runs Read GTA. He's played the series since GTA III came out, followed by Vice City and San Andreas, which he still plays to this day. He's most interested in the technical side of the games and he built the platform Read GTA runs on.

The leaders of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga, under the lights at the Emirates. That’s the kind of Champions League night we waited years for, and now it’s a regular Tuesday. The champions are six points clear at home, unbeaten in Europe and up against a Dortmund side that hasn’t lost a league game all season.

There’s a twist, though. David Raya is out, so Kepa gets the gloves, and Saturday’s 2-2 at St James’ Park showed that this team can still be got at. This Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund preview covers everything you need before the 8pm kick-off. That means the latest odds, team news for both sides, predicted line-ups, the head-to-head record, the key stats and our prediction and betting tips.

The bookies make Arsenal strong favourites, as you’d expect with this home record in Europe. Dortmund are big outsiders for a side that’s top of the Bundesliga, and that tells you how highly the market rates the Gunners at the Emirates. Prices were checked on matchday and will move once the team sheets are out, so always check before you bet.

Those prices make Arsenal roughly a 67% chance, with the draw around 19% and Dortmund around 14% once the bookmaker margin is stripped out.

Be careful with the scorer lists, because some bookmakers still have Martin Zubimendi priced up and he’s injured.

The big news is in goal. Raya came off with a shoulder problem at Newcastle and Arteta confirmed he won’t be fit for tonight, though he said it “doesn’t look too serious” and surgery isn’t needed. Kepa Arrizabalaga steps in.

Missing Saka is a blow, but Madueke has stepped up brilliantly. He rescued a point at Newcastle and Arteta called him “decisive” in his press conference. Zubimendi’s absence means Myles Lewis-Skelly is the most likely option to partner Declan Rice in midfield.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapié; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.

Saliba being back is a big boost, and there’s a real chance he comes straight in. Havertz is also pushing for a start up front.

Dortmund had two big worries going into this one, and both look like they’ve cleared. Kovač said Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka trained on Monday and are “ready for tomorrow’s match”. Guirassy missed the weekend win at Gladbach with a hamstring problem, so whether he’s fit enough to start is still a question.

Our very own Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Dortmund and is allowed to play against us. He hasn’t started a game since mid-October, so expect him on the bench. It would be very Arsenal for him to come off it and score, so let’s hope not.

Kobel; Anton, Schlotterbeck, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Nmecha, Bellingham, Svensson; Beier, Karetsas; Silva.

If Guirassy is fit to start, he comes in for Silva. He’s scored four goals in four Champions League games this season, so he’s the man to watch.

Arsenal and Dortmund have met eight times in competitive football, all in the Champions League group stage. Arsenal have won four, Dortmund three, and one has been a draw.

Don’t read too much into the friendly in August. It’s the competitive record that counts, and Dortmund have won just once in their last eight trips to England.

Arsenal have scored eight and conceded only three in Europe this season, with three of their four games away from home. Dortmund have scored seven and conceded five, and they haven’t kept a clean sheet in the Champions League yet.

Arsenal are top of the Premier League on 28 points from 11 games, six clear of Brighton. Saturday’s draw at Newcastle ended a five-match winning run in the league. Eze put us ahead, Newcastle turned it around after the break, and Madueke got us out of jail.

Dortmund are unbeaten in ten Bundesliga games and sit two points clear of Bayern. They’ve conceded only seven league goals, the fewest in Germany, and Felix Nmecha’s goal at Gladbach on Saturday took them back above Bayern. They also showed a bit of fight by drawing late at Bayern in October, although they let a 2-0 lead slip at home to Werder Bremen.

Four straight clean sheets at home in the Champions League is serious form. But Dortmund nearly always score, and with Kepa in goal instead of Raya there’s a bit more risk. The safer way to back an Arsenal win is to pair it with under 3.5 goals rather than paying 4/11 for a straight win. The 2-0 at 11/2 is a decent shout for anyone wanting a bigger price.

He’s the most likely scorer on the night, and Dortmund’s back line hasn’t kept a clean sheet in Europe all season. For those who like the shots markets, Gyökeres to have two or more shots on target at 8/5 is worth a look too.

This is a closer call than it looks. Dortmund score in nearly every game, but Arsenal haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe. If Saliba comes back in, BTTS no at odds-against becomes even more attractive.

Arsenal to win, under 3.5 goals and Gyökeres to score. That fits a 2-0 or 2-1 win, which is exactly the kind of result we’d expect.

Arsenal at 4/11 isn’t much of a price as a single, so plenty of Gooners will be tying the win into a bigger slip. This is a two-night matchday, with more games tomorrow, so there’s plenty to choose from. If you want ideas for the rest of the round, the football accumulators site lists acca picks for both nights of Champions League action, sorted by market and price. You’ll find selections across match result, double chance, both teams to score, goals lines and scorer markets. Prices are checked every two hours, there’s a public results log, and it doesn’t take bets itself, so you still pick your own bookmaker. The picks come from bookmaker prices and not from the team news, so do your own checks, especially on a night when Raya is out.

Our advice is to keep your acca short. Arsenal look a safe enough leg, but adding too many short-priced selections can turn a good bet into a bad one.

Dortmund are a good side and they’ll fancy their chances with Guirassy back. Their press could make life uncomfortable for Kepa early on. But Arsenal are unbeaten in 19 Champions League games and haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe, and Dortmund’s away record in England is poor.

We expect Arsenal to be patient, dominate the ball and grind out a win that puts us right in the mix for a top-two finish in the league phase. Madueke and Gyökeres look the most likely men to make the difference.

Prediction. Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund.

The game is live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK.

Arsenal are around 4/11 to win, the draw is about 4/1 and Dortmund are around 13/2 to 7/1.

No. Raya is out with a shoulder injury, so Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in goal.

Yes. Nwaneri is on loan at Dortmund from Arsenal and is allowed to face his parent club.

In eight competitive meetings, Arsenal have won four, Dortmund three and one has been drawn. The last competitive game was a 2-0 Arsenal win at the Emirates in November 2014.

#1954. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#1953. Bowen’s West Ham Future | We’ve Been Here Before

West Ham United captain Jarrod Bowen has revealed that he will sit down with the club to discuss his future at the end of the season should the Hammers fail to secure promotion. The England international insists he never wanted to leave following relegation and remains determined to get West Ham back into the Premier League.

However, speaking in an interview with Sam Tabuteau for The Standard, Bowen made it clear that another conversation would be necessary if the promotion bid failed.

With Scott Parker’s team languishing in 13th position ahead of tomorrow’s visit of Stoke City, Bowen’s latest admission is particularly significant. After six games without a win, the prospect of West Ham spending another season in the Championship is becoming increasingly realistic.

As far as I’m concerned, nobody could blame Jarrod Bowen for leaving West Ham. The truth of the matter is that I wouldn’t have held it against him had he decided to move in the summer. After all, he’s given everything for this football club.

I also think it’s important to state on these pages that whilst I don’t particularly believe him to be captain material, that in no way clouds my view of him as a player. Bowen is already somebody I would consider to be a West Ham legend.

Let’s be fair, there are plenty who have achieved icon status at this football club without having done a quarter of what Jarrod has in claret and blue.

Kretinsky and Bowen in Prague as the skipper committed to life in the Championship

I do find it intriguing that Bowen is once again talking about sitting down with the club at the end of the season. It was only in the summer that Jarrod flew over to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský and do precisely that.

One can only imagine what assurances Bowen was given during that meeting to persuade him to stay. And I wouldn’t be an inquisitive Hammers fan if I didn’t wonder whether the recruitment since then has lived up to the ambition outlined to him of building a Championship-winning team.

Personally, I’ll take the talk of another meeting with a pinch of salt. I can’t see any way Bowen plays a second season in the Championship, and nor should he.

It’s always been my suspicion that failing to secure promotion at the first attempt would likely result in an extended stay in the lower division.

And quite frankly, Bowen is better than that.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#1951. Arsenal waste chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back to claim Emirates point

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

Despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and quickly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

Despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

Arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player quickly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

Continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

Despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

Although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.

#1950. Arsenal injury latest: Arteta faces selection headache as crucial fixtures approach

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could not have been in a more difficult position to suffer multiple key player injuries. Mikel Arteta will face a busy period with a Manchester City visit to the Emirates on Sunday and then in December face Tottenham and Real Madrid.

Although David Raya, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are all sidelined due to injury, Arteta has separate issues to deal with for each. However, the timing of their injuries is especially annoying.

The good news is that William Saliba is back in contention. But Arsenal can’t expect a select group of players to magically fix all of their issues. Over the coming weeks the true strength of the squad will be put to the test.

Raya is currently the most affected player. He suffered a shoulder injury while challenging William Osula in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle. As a result, he was also absent for the Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.

Whilst there had been initial concerns over how long Raya would be out for, scans showed that there was no need for him to undergo surgery. Arteta has called the preliminary reports positive. However, he has yet to state if Raya will play against City.

Kepa Arrizabalaga has stepped in for Dortmund, but Arsenal are affected by the absence of their preferred keeper. Raya is reliable and composed and has great passing ability.

These attributes will be of value especially when facing City’s potent attack. Although Kepa has top-level experience, it is by no means a game that Arteta would prefer to be playing with an unstable goalkeeping situation.

Raya may be available again either on November 29 or when facing Brentford on December 2. Much will hinge on the progress of his shoulder in the days ahead.

Arguably, though, Saka’s injury represents a bigger worry. He was sidelined after hurting his quadriceps in a match against Bayern Munich on 21st October.

Arteta has previously suggested that it will take around eight weeks for Saka to make a full recovery. 20th December provides a possible return date, but there are no assurances that he will be fit to play at this time.

We have already analysed how important Saka is to Arsenal – both as a creator and in scoring and providing width. The new right winger will need to be able to create key moments in close games.

As well as losing Saka, Zubimendi is also set to be out for a number of weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem during his Spain duty. He may be available for the December 13 game against Bournemouth.

Without Zubimendi, Arteta will need to make further decisions regarding his midfield. Like Saka, Zubimendi is good at maintaining good structure, and this is key to Arsenal’s game. Finding a suitable replacement will not be an easy task.

There is some good news. Saliba has overcome his back issue and is once again in the squad. In addition, Max Dowman has served his 3-game ban.

Saliba’s return is particularly timely with City’s attacking threat heading to the Emirates. Arsenal need stability at centre-back, especially if Raya is unavailable.

Arteta still has decisions to make. Although there is not a great deal of time, Arsenal do not always find suitable substitutes. The squad is deep enough to still challenge, it will be in these next games that it will become apparent how much Arsenal miss key players.

#1948. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

"He's important for us"Virgil van Dijk says Cody Gakpo will be important for Liverpool this season after the win over Ipswich 💪 pic.twitter.com/XLWfxbpK2d

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

2 - Liverpool have now won as many Premier League away games by 2+ goals this season (1) as they did in the whole of last season (2-0 v West Ham in November 2025).Lift-off. pic.twitter.com/rp39p6C8z5
