#1923. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

Newcastle are in their iconic black and white strip, while Bournemouth are sporting an eye-catching purple away kit. We are just minutes away from kick-off. St James’ Park is in full voice.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of the two line-ups.

In for his home debut! 😍🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/yqAQpT9vjH

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

They can be forgiven if they feel tired this morning.

The talented 23-year-old was the subject of interest from the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United and Chelsea in the summer, but Bournemouth managed to keep a hold of him, despite the midfielder rejecting the opportunity to sign a new contract at the club.

With his current deal expiring in 2028, Scott has made an excellent start to this season, and scored a brilliant opener in Bournemouth’s 1-1 draw with Everton last weekend.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernandez-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment team, “the one”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1922. Liverpool like Dortmund sensation Joane Gadou but they haven’t answered ongoing worry

Liverpool are among Premier League clubs keeping a close eye on young defensive talent Joane Gadou, reports Mark Brus.

The Borussia Dortmund centre-back (19) signed for the Bundesliga giants this summer and has featured 17 times for them since (across all competitions).

Reporting for CaughtOffside’s The Daily Briefing, Mark Brus said: “I’m reliably told by sources with ties to the agents industry that Arsenal and other Premier League clubs have been closely monitoring Gadou for some time. The Frenchman only joined Dortmund this summer after impressing at Red Bull Salzburg, and he also had a spell in PSG’s academy earlier in his career.”

He went on to add that a source mentioned: “Arsenal got a close look at him yesterday, but the reality is that they have been monitoring Gadou for months. A lot of the top clubs know about him, even if they weren’t ready to move for him yet. I see him developing at Dortmund for a bit longer, but it’s clear how talented he is and if he carries on like this they won’t hold on to him for long.”

Liverpool, Manchester United and Real Madrid are ‘keen’ on Gadou, but may have to come up against competition from PSG if the player continues his current developmental trajectory.

And that should come as no surprise to onlookers when the Frenchman is putting in top-quality displays of the calibre he produced against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Combative, solid in the air, and against Mikel Arteta’s tricky Premier League champions. Notably, this hardly seems a fluke either, judging by the kind of numbers Joane Gadou is putting up for Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

* Joane Gadou’s stats in the 2026/27 Bundesliga season (via FotMob)

Between Giovanni Leoni, Jeremy Jacquet, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, high-potential, young centre-backs are hardly in short supply at L4.

That’s not to say there’s never any justification for adding more talent to the club ranks, but the problem Liverpool are facing at the end of the 2026/27 season dictates that the club should be looking at experienced operators.

As things currently stand, Virgil van Dijk has no clear idea whether he’s staying or going in the summer, and there’s yet to be any kind of guarantee around Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo.

We strongly suspect that Liverpool will have serious conversations about the Dutchman and his Uruguayan teammate given the pair’s strong performances this term. However, there remains a possibility that the Reds could be left incredibly short on experienced heads by the summer transfer window.

If that’s the case, this should be an absolute priority at the back over landing someone of Gadou’s profile.

#1921. Man United must build on improved Sporting Lisbon display in vital Premier League clash with Brentford

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:51, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:55

Manchester United will continue their Premier League campaign against Brentford on Saturday afternoon, and Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law has discussed all of the latest talking points surrounding the 20-time English champions.

Man United conceded the most goals, 36, the most penalties, five, and the most red cards, five, of any Premier League team this season.

The Liverpool game was controversial as well, with the red card for Leny Yoro that has since been rescinded. Isak does not have even a little bit of control of the ball. He has ballooned it 10 metres in front of him, and still, he is given the red card for that one.

That was a huge turning moment in the game. That is not to say that United should be going on and losing 4-0 at Anfield, even with 10 men, but it is a game-changing incident.

It leaves United on one Premier League win this season, down in 19th spot in the table, eight points from 11 games, which is absolutely horrendous. What I would say is it was a tough start for Pochettino. It was a big game at Anfield against the Liverpool side that played well.

If you concede that red card and then the fact they score from the free kick, that is a real hammer blow, and then you have to hold on and try to keep it 1-0 going into the second half.

United could not do that. The performance level was well off it again. They conceded four goals in each of their last two Premier League games. It is 23 goals conceded now in the Premier League in 11 games.

This team just cannot keep clean sheets for love nor money, in the Premier League, in any competition. Not kept a clean sheet since the win over Sabah in the Champions League, their first Champions League game in the league phase.

If you keep a clean sheet, you have got a really good chance of winning football games. If you concede two a game, three a game, you are just not going to pick up wins.

The game against Sporting Lisbon was one we could do a two-hour podcast on. The first penalty against Sporting is very soft.

If that is a penalty then we might as well pack up and do podcasts on something else, because I do not want to be a part of a game that says that is a penalty. The Senne Lammens one is a penalty. What is he doing? He is flying out.

Then the goal that was disallowed for Amad, how that is a foul from Tielemans I will never know. An absolute horrific decision. The Fernandes penalty is a penalty for me.

I think it is a straightforward decision. I do not think it is a foul on Senne Lammens, and I also do not think it is a foul for the last goal.

Dorgu got penalised for jumping into the goalkeeper, but they are either both fouls or neither are fouls. The contact on Senne Lammens for the Sporting equaliser was soft. I do not think that should be disallowed.

I do not think the United goal should be disallowed. The late red card was clumsy from Tielemans. It is not vintage football, it is not vintage Man United. They struggled in the final third of the field. Zirkzee came into the side and did okay.

An interesting stat from that game was that United had 12 high turnovers against Sporting, their most in any game this season.

It did feel like they were winning the ball back higher. They were definitely pressing more as a unit. The shape of the team was better. They need a centre forward. If they had had Sesko last night and that threat in behind, you feel like they could have picked up all three points.

They were decent on the ball, recovered well from going behind in the game. Sporting are a good side and have had good results in the Champions League this season.

They are a really strong team with really good players. There were positives from the Sporting Lisbon game, and it leaves them in a decent enough position in the Champions League.

They need to beat Leipzig in the next European game if they are really going to push on. They have got Bayern Munich and Villarreal as well, and those are going to be difficult games.

From the Champions League point of view, I still think they are in a decent enough position to finish in, whether that is the automatic qualification places or ultimately the play-offs.

Dealing with the Premier League is where they need to focus. They have got three games in a row now before the Leipzig game: Brentford, Newcastle away, Coventry at home.

The next two home games are absolutely massive. If they get turned over here and then go to Newcastle and do not manage to get a win, and then Coventry pick something up against them, it is very difficult.

I do not think United are getting relegated this season. I say that out of hope. I think they are going to be busy in January. They are going to have to be inventive.

Around £50m is the figure they are going to have to spend. They need to bring in three players: definitely a striker, definitely a centre-back, definitely a full-back.

Carlos Baleba is going to be back sooner than expected. They are going to hope to get Rashford back at some stage in the not-too-distant future. Those two did train in the gym ahead of the Sporting game. Shaw was back on the bench as well.

Pochettino said he was proud of his players for their performance level in the Sporting game and for overcoming the adversity, because there were some really horrific decisions from the referee and VAR in that game.

United have not had the rub of the green. With the Fernandes goal and the divot, they showed the earlier clip and it was Fernandes himself who had made that divot in the turf.

He had had a heavy touch with his boot in the box, and they circled back and it was the one he had made. So he actually managed to assist himself with that bobble. There has been a lot that has gone against United this season.

This is a really big game on Saturday afternoon and one I am hoping they can win against Brentford. First Premier League win for Pochettino. Go to the Newcastle game, can you get a point? Can you go there and beat Coventry? Can you beat Leipzig? Football changes very quickly. If you put three or four good results together, everyone feels different.

It goes in cycles. A big football match. Brentford, it is one of those games that back in the day, United at home to Brentford, you would think it is a gimme, a home win.

But they are an excellent team, Brentford, sitting sixth in the table at the moment with 17 points. Going away from home brings its different challenges, and without Igor Thiago as well is a big one.

I did also want to mention Senne Lammens' form, which is a concern for me.

Going back to the middle of September, Paul Scholes said in a podcast, The Good, The Bad and the Football, that he questioned whether Lammens was good enough, at a stage when he was actually playing quite well.

And I have to be honest, I am in that camp now. He is making a lot of mistakes.

There was one in the Sporting game last night where they did not concede from it, but he pushed the ball back into the middle and no one was on the rebound to put it away. The mistake for the second goal was a big one as well.

His form is slightly concerning and his confidence looks shot at the moment. I think he starts here, but it will be interesting to see whether United ultimately think they might have to get another goalkeeper in at some stage.

#1919. “Why didn’t they check?” – Pochettino still fuming over refereeing decision in Liverpool romp

Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity. The red card has since been overturned on the basis that the Reds striker was unlikely to get to the ball had he not been impeded.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

“[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

“[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

Replays show that it was actually Fernandes who pushed Barcola out of the way when the ball was struck, and the Liverpool forward most certainly isn’t at fault for how poorly the Man United defensive wall was set up.

Bruno literally pushed Barcola into the wall 😂😂😂😂 these lot are losing the plot.pic.twitter.com/tjPFU56OTg https://t.co/bJWXQfmfUk

Even though his team were very much discommoded by the early red card, their response to that setback was still a meek surrender, and that’s what should concern their head coach the most rather than blaming opposition players.

The Red Devils still had more than 80 minutes to reorganise and try to get a result, and while they did stem the tide for a large chunk of the game at 2-0, they were still indebted to wasteful finishing from the home side that the final score wasn’t even more emphatic.

While Pochettino moans, Liverpool will be busy preparing for their own Champions League clash away to Club Brugge, followed by the small matter of the Merseyside derby on Sunday.

#1918. Real Betis vs Rayo Vallecano - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 20:17, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:19

Real Betis will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume domestic affairs at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday afternoon.

The Seville outfit lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 21 victories to Rayo's 13, while 16 of their 50 previous matches have finished all square.

Real Betis will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-0 win over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, with the result leaving them sixth in the overall table, claiming 12 points from their five games in the league stage of the tournament.

Manuel Pellegrini's side boast a record of eight wins, three draws and two defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 27 points leaving them in fourth spot in the La Liga table, five points ahead of fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

Real Betis are only four points behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, but they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sevilla in the Seville derby last weekend.

El Glorioso were last victorious in the league on November 8, beating Elche 2-0, while their last defeat at this level was a 5-2 home reverse to Barcelona on October 17.

Real Betis will be in Copa del Rey action against CD Extremadura on December 1 before facing Atletico Madrid in La Liga ahead of their next Champions League fixture with Como.

Rayo, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of successive defeats to Real Sociedad and Valencia in Spain's top flight, and it has been a tough season to date for the capital outfit.

Benat San Jose's side have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches to sit in 16th spot in the division on 12 points, level on points with 18th-placed Getafe.

Rayo have the third-worst away record in Spain's top flight this season, picking up just two points from six matches, which is a concern ahead of this game.

Los Franjirrojos have actually drawn their last four matches against Real Betis, while they have not been beaten by the Seville outfit since September 2023.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw in the corresponding game during the 2025-26 campaign, and it was also 1-1 when they locked horns in the same stadium in December 2024.

Real Betis remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension, while Dani Ceballos, Giovani Lo Celso, Iker Losada and Jose Morante are out through injury.

Cucho Hernandez scored twice against Slovan Bratislava on his return from injury on Tuesday evening, and the 27-year-old is now set to come in for his first league appearance since the middle of October.

Antony and Isco are both set to retain their spots in the final third of the field, while Pablo Fornals is likely to be joined by Marc Roca in the middle of the midfield.

As for Rayo, Augusto Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin are out through injury, but the capital outfit have no fresh fitness concerns.

Sergio Camello has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 13 appearances, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be another spot at centre-forward for Randy Nteka despite the fact that the 28-year-old is still waiting for his first goal of the campaign.

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Hernandez

Audero; Ratiu, Lejeune, Sadick, Tsiaishvili; Palazon, Ciss, Lopez, De Frutos; Nteka, Camello

Rayo have found it difficult on their travels this season, and we are expecting Real Betis to secure all three points even though their preparation time for the match will be short.

#1917. Andoni Iraola has rightly ‘enjoyed’ watching Club Brugge this season – and Liverpool must beware

Andoni Iraola has said that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

The Liverpool head coach said (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

“With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also big, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

“I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

“I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

Iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

Regis Le Bris will be under pressure to pick up all three points when Sunderland host Tottenham on 29 November.

The Black Cats have been struggling to find results in the Premier League, and have ultimately left themselves in the relegation zone.

The Sunderland boss will need to make some difficult selection decisions, particularly if he is to get the better of a Tottenham side arriving in strong form.

Brian Brobbey's injury is still set to keep him out of action for Sunderland until after this weekend.

#1915. Moreirense vs Santa Clara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are currently some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary issues against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose issue.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

A Ferreira; Pinto, Kevyn Monteiro, Batista, A Martinez; N John, Liberato; Andrade, Mendonca, Landerson; Vonic

Franca; Lucas Soares, Ythallo, H Silva, Fofana; Tavares, Borges, Vasconcelos; V Lopes, Paciencia, B Lucas

Santa Clara have been considerably stronger away from home this season, but their defensive absences could prove costly against a Moreirense side that have won three of the last four meetings between the clubs.

Furthermore, the hosts have an opportunity to exploit an inexperienced centre-back pairing, although their own scoring problems and the visitors' impressive away record suggest neither side will have enough to claim all three points.

#1914. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

#1908. Real Madrid's £68m Nico Paz transfer plan faces fresh uncertainty as Jose Mourinho responds

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.

The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.

Madrid retained the option to bring Paz back in the summer of 2027 when an agreement was reached with Como in June to allow the 22-year-old to continue his development in Serie A. However, despite recent suggestions that the Spanish giants have already decided to exercise that option, uncertainty remains over their plans.

Asked about Paz during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, Mourinho offered a typically brief response: "He's not my player."

The Portuguese manager's reluctance to discuss a player contracted to another club should not be interpreted as opposition to the transfer, although his response offered little clarification following contrasting reports in the Spanish media.

Cadena COPE reported last week that Real Madrid intended to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option next summer, with Como having reportedly been informed of the decision.

However, according to Jose Felix Diaz of AS, Madrid have yet to reach a definitive conclusion and could wait until the spring before deciding whether to bring their former academy prospect back.

The club's official statement in June confirmed the existence of a unilateral buy-back option for the 2027-28 season. Crucially, the agreement allowing Paz to remain in Italy for another year was reached at the player's own request, underlining the importance he attaches to regular first-team football at this stage of his career.

The biggest sporting consideration for Madrid remains the presence of Jude Bellingham, whose performances under Mourinho have strengthened his position as the team's principal attacking midfielder.

The England international has scored seven goals and provided five assists in 18 appearances this season, including a goal and an assist in Tuesday's 5-1 victory over PSV. Madrid are also reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new contract for Bellingham, whose existing agreement runs until 2029.

Paz's versatility would give Mourinho some scope to accommodate both players. The Argentine is capable of operating from the right or in a slightly deeper midfield position, although those roles would bring him into direct competition with Arda Guler, Brahim Diaz and Bernardo Silva.

Madrid must also consider how the squad will look next season, with Rodrygo expected to return from injury and Franco Mastantuono due back from his loan spell. Summer signing Yan Diomande represents another significant investment in the attacking department.

Spending £68m on Paz could still make considerable financial sense given his age, development and potential resale value. However, the circumstances that prompted him to remain at Como last summer have hardly changed, particularly with Bellingham enjoying such an influential role under Mourinho.

Waiting until the spring would allow Madrid to assess both Paz's progress and the needs of their own squad before committing to a substantial expenditure. With their final buy-back opportunity approaching, the Spanish giants must determine whether they can offer the Argentine the regular football that has allowed him to flourish in Italy.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will be pleased by his side's home record given they have won two of their five top-flight fixtures at Home Deluxe Arena while only being beaten twice.

Schalke could view their goalless stalemate with Stuttgart on November 21 positively, especially as it arrested a four-match losing streak.

However, it would be understandable if boss Miron Muslic was feeling pressure given he has failed to oversee a victory in eight games, with his side losing on five occasions.

The visitors might take comfort from the fact they have beaten their hosts in their two most recent meetings, the latest of which was a 3-2 success in the 2. Bundesliga in April 2026.

Die Knappen rank 18th in the division for goals scored (five), though only Borussia Dortmund (seven), Bayern Munich (10) and Freiburg (10) have conceded fewer times (11).

Schalke's form on the road has been poor considering they are winless in their last four away outings, suffering three losses.

Paderborn will be unable to call upon defenders Marcel Hoffmeier (muscle) and Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant (ankle), as well as forward Timur Gayret (knee).

Jano ter Horst, Tjark Scheller and Mattes Hansen have been regulars in the backline, and they are set to protect goalkeeper Nahuel Noll.

Stefano Marino and Marvin Pieringer are likely to be trusted as a front two, and they will be keen to improve upon their tallies of two and one league goal respectively.

Schalke's absentee list is extensive, with defender Timo Becker, midfielder Ron Schallenberg and forward Emil Hojlund three of seven injured stars.

Vitalie Becker will start in the backline, Soufian El-Faouzi is likely to anchor the middle of the pitch and Moussa Sylla is certain to lead the frontline.

Perhaps the most likely outcome is a stalemate, especially as neither have proven to be particularly productive in the final third.

#1902. Iraola will be wincing as Liverpool dealt worrying injury setback in first half against Brugge

Liverpool have been dealt a fresh injury concern in the first half of their Champions League fixture against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds got off to a strong start at the Jan Breydel Stadium as they pounced on a loose pass by Yann Sommer to take the lead through a close-range finish from Alexander Isak.

However, Andoni Iraola was left wincing in the technical area when, shortly before half-time, Victor Munoz went to ground and stayed there after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area was abruptly halted.

It quickly became clear that the Liverpool winger was in pain, and a stretcher was readied before the Spaniard got to his feet and was able to limp off, with Rio Ngumoha coming on in his place (Sky Sports).

(Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The sight of Munoz standing up and walking (gingerly) off the pitch came as a relief, but to lose the 23-year-old in such innocuous circumstances represents a big body blow to Liverpool.

The summer signing from Osasuna has had to rely mostly on substitute appearances so far in his Reds career, but he was handed a start by Iraola tonight off the back of his fine showing off the bench against Manchester United on Sunday.

The Spanish winger rounded off the scoring in that match and had Club Brugge terrified with some mazy, proactive dribbling before that unfortunate injury setback when he overstretched to try and get to the ball.

It remains to be seen just how seriously Munoz has been hurt and whether he’ll face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, but we can only keep our fingers crossed that it isn’t as bad as what it initially seemed.

Manchester United failed to recover after two first-half Callum Wilson goals helped to condemn them to a 4-0 defeat to Brentford.

Mauricio Pochettino's side flew out of the blocks in the second half on Saturday, 28 November, but it was all for nothing at Old Trafford.

Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added third and fourth goals late in the game, as Keith Andrews' side rose to fifth in the Premier League table.

At the other end of the table, the Red Devils remain sitting 19th in the standings, with a crisis truly emerging for the Red Devils.

The atmosphere was toxic right from kick-off, and by the end, Old Trafford was almost silent after the majority of fans walked out before full-time.

Football Insider has taken a look at some things that supporters may have missed during the 90 minutes at the Theatre of Dreams.

Supporters loved Michael Carrick right until the end of his tenure, and they continue to show their respect, despite Pochettino now being in charge.

The players are under pressure to perform on the pitch, with the club currently in a very tricky position in the Premier League table.

Of all players, you would expect Bruno Fernandes to keep his cool and encourage his teammates, but after Joshua Zirkzee attempted and failed a flick, that couldn't be further from the truth.

Clearly, the roof isn't the only leaky thing at Old Trafford.

Dango Ouattara skipped past the centre-back, but he was cautioned anyway for the incident, and now he's suspended for the trip to Newcastle United on Wednesday, 2 December.

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:14

Separated by just two points around the top eight of the Championship table, Queens Park Rangers and Sheffield United will square off at MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday.

The hosts sit seventh having extended an unbeaten streak with an away draw in midweek, while their visitors sit a point off the playoff spots after a win and a draw of their own since the international break.

Queens Park Rangers return to MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday with the hopes of extending an unbeaten run in the Championship and strengthening their position in the top eight.

In their second season under Julien Stephan, following a 15th-placed finish last time around, they currently find themselves seventh having earned 28 points from their first 17 outings, winning seven and only losing three of those with only league leaders Middlesbrough suffering fewer defeats.

The Hoops' success has largely come at the back, with only three teams conceding fewer than the 19 goals they have allowed, four of which came in an away defeat to Southampton at the end of October.

Stephan's men bounced back and headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against Burnley and a win over Lincoln City, before returning with a 1-0 away victory at Millwall at the weekend and a 1-1 draw against in-form Norwich City at Carrow Road on Tuesday having led through Harvey Vale.

With confidence to take from their return from the recent break, but just two points ahead of their visitors in the battle for playoff places, QPR will bid to make it five games unbeaten and bounce back to winning ways on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to the capital aiming to break into the playoff spots having also enjoyed a positive return from the international break.

After a slow start to their third straight Championship campaign, in which they set out to battle for promotion, Sheffield United seemingly hit their stride after the September and October international break, moving onto 22 points from 14 games with four wins and just one loss in a six-game span.

They would then go into the second break of the term on the back of a disappointing loss away at strugglers Charlton Athletic but bounced back in style on their return last weekend, hosting Watford and dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz had them two up with an early brace and Jordan Ayew and Sydie Peck added second-half goals.

Southampton then visited Bramall Lane on Tuesday, and Chris Wilder's men looked to fall short to a solitary Lewis Dobbin goal, but they were eventually able to level and take a share of the spoils as Peck equalised in the 90th minute.

Now poised to crack the playoff spots with some momentum behind them, having earned 17 points in their last nine matches, Sheffield United sit just one point outside the top eight and two off Saturday's hosts, and they will hope to leapfrog QPR with another victory at the weekend.

QPR remain without defender Amadou Mbengue, who is sidelined with a long-term injury, while Jimmy Dunne should also miss out again having been absent for their last two games.

In Dunne's absence, Jake Clarke-Salter and Ronnie Edwards should partner up at the heart of a back four, while Nicolas Madsen also missed the trip to Norwich meaning Glen Kamara and Jonathan Varane will likely continue their midfield pairing.

Richard Kone and Rumarn Burrell will compete to lead the line, while Ilias Chair will hope to return from the outset in support after Kwame Poku, Harvey Vale and Koki Saito were preferred behind Burrell in midweek.

Sheffield United defender Femi Seriki is ruled out for the season through injury, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One, Joe Rothwell and Jamie Shackleton will likely remain sidelined.

They have two players returning, though, with Japhet Tanganga back available after suspension and the captain set to rejoin Liam Kitching at centre-back, and Ben Brereton Diaz back in contention for an attacking spot after being ineligible to play against parent club Southampton in midweek.

He could take the place of Jordan Ayew, who may be rested after being withdrawn as a precaution on Tuesday following two impressive displays, with Tyrese Campbell and Patrick Bamford also pushing to come in up top, while Kalvin Phillips will hope to return to the starting XI in midfield alongside Sydie Peck.

#1899. Paul Robinson got it badly wrong, Daniel Farke answers 'huge Leeds concern'

Correspondent AUTHORITY Sports journalist with experience at GamingINTEL and GRV Media; University of Wolverhampton graduate. FOCUS Data content, opinion, and general news coverage across the Breaking Media network. THE INSIGHT Scott utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, broad-spectrum reporting. Paul Robinson's criticism of Daniel Farke has aged like milk after Leeds United defeated Coventry City 3-0.

The Whites are in terrific form, winning three Premier League games on the bounce for the first time since 2020-21.

Victory against the Sky Blues will leave the Elland Road side in the top half of the Premier League at the end of this game week, no matter the results elsewhere.

Farke's side have managed to score eight goals, while only conceding once over this stretch.

That represents a remarkable turnaround for a side that had been struggling for consistency just weeks ago.

With Robinson now having egg on his face thanks to the latest performances from Farke's side.

The criticism that Leeds lacked the attacking quality to trouble Premier League opponents has quickly been put to bed

And Robinson's assessment of the Whites looks worse as the weeks go on.

Speaking on Sky Sports back after Leeds' 2-0 loss to Bournemouth on 31 October, Robinson felt that Leeds' firepower up top was lacking, and would ultimately hurt their season.

He stated: "Leeds are playing too many games like they don’t want to lose."

Before going on to say: "They are not scoring goals. But once Bournemouth scored, they never looked like scoring. That’s a huge concern for Daniel Farke."

However, now his claim has been made to look premature, and ultimately foolish.

Over this three-game win streak, culminating in that win over Coventry, the Whites are averaging 2.5 xG per game, as per FotMob.

And it is not like they have been playing poor teams either, with Chelsea and Tottenham part of that run.

The Whites have also averaged 5.6 big chances created per game, with two clean sheets.

Proving to be capable on both ends of the pitch as they go in search of the big dream of qualifying for Europe.

The test for Farke now is if he can repeat the trick at Leeds.

Leeds have shown they can beat the Premier League's top sides with wins over Chelsea and Spurs, and have passed tests against the newly promoted sides.

Over the next three games, that will be the defining factor as to whether the Whites have turned a corner.

Coming up for them are away trips to face Manchester City and Liverpool, while a home tie against Ipswich Town is sandwiched in between.

If they come out of that with more positive results, then Leeds fans' European dream would grow even closer to reality.

#1897. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...
