Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.

Possession: Arsenal 58%-42% ChelseaShots: 10-6Shots on target: 6-3Corners: 2-0Touches in opposition box: 26-13

A really enjoyable half of football, even if it was slowed down a little in the last few minutes by a series of niggly fouls. Arsenal are the better team here but Chelsea are definitely dangerous. That Neto shot off the post was evidence of how quickly they can hurt the Arsenal defence.

The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

Chelsea hit the post late on in the half. Chelsea counter from inside their own half and Pedro whips a ball first time down the right channel to pick out the run of Neto. The Portuguese forward drives at Gabriel inside the Arsenal box and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot. His effort comes back off the far post and Chelsea were inches away from retaking the lead.

That left side of the Arsenal defence again. Wide open for Neto to run into the space. Chelsea looking for the early ball every time.

Tensions are boiling over as Lavia and White come to blows. As Lavia shepherds the ball out of play, White threw himself to ground and wanted a free-kick. Lavia is not impressed by White’s antics and lets him know about it.

Is Palmer in some trouble? Raya catches a free-kick into his box and gets Arsenal going on the counter with a long ball forward. With Havertz getting away from him, Palmer brings him down and takes the yellow. There was another covering defender, hence why it was just a yellow.

As we approach half-time, there have been 15 shots in total from both sides in the game with nine of those being on target.

Chelsea win it just inside the Arsenal half after good defensive work from Lavia and Pedro then spots Raya off his line. The Chelsea forward therefore opts to shoot from a long way out but drags his effort wide.

White and Havertz exchange a neat one-two down Arsenal’s right, with the latter clipping the ball to the back post. Lavia, with Saka right behind him, heads away well under pressure.

That is a decent opportunity for Rogers to get his second of the game. Pedro lays it off to him on the left side of the box and Rogers tries to curl one into the far corner but it goes wide.

Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Once again, though, they look suspect in defence. The Havertz equaliser could have been stopped twice, but Chelsea defence just did not react. Fofana let Havertz past and Odegaard set a bit of a screen that stopped Lacroix getting close.

Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

Against his former club, Havertz gets the equaliser but again there will be an offside check. It appears he is onside as he receives the ball on the right. Havertz then drives across the face of the penalty area and shoots towards the near post. Martinez should make the save but can only palm it into the corner of the net. The goal stands and it is 1-1 at the Emirates.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

I think we’d be talking about Robert Sanchez if he had let that Havertz shot in at his near post. That wasn’t great from Martinez and Arsenal fans will love reminding him of it. Great game, this.

James decides to shoot from range and he strikes it really well, forcing Raya into a good save. Arsenal then counter and it ends with Odegaard having a shot blocked. Should Havertz have shot himself rather than lay it off for Odegaard?

Back come Chelsea and Pedro nearly gets on the end of a cross from Palmer.

Palmer, who has been quiet so far, receives it on the edge of the box and he is afforded too much space. He decides to shoot and looks to curl it into the far corner but Raya gets down to his right to make the save. He had to make sure he did not spill it as Pedro was lurking.

Tzolis cross from the left having been found by a great ball from Odegaard finds Havertz near the edge of the box. Fofana makes a crucial block to deny Havertz but Arsenal have the corner out on the left. Once more, Chelsea leave plenty of players up the pitch and Fofana heads away.

Odegaard works it to Saka on the right side of the box and the latter strikes towards goal, forcing Martinez into a decent save.

The goal will not stand. Konsa was offside before Calafiori scored so Chelsea remain 1-0 up.

#ARSCHE – 12' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of goal – and determined that Konsa was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was disallowed.

The hosts equalise with a set-piece. Pedro should clear Rice’s free-kick but completely misses it. The ball comes to Gabriel, whose shot is saved by Martinez. Konsa then hits the post before a mad scramble ensues. Calafiori then forces the ball into the net. However, VAR are checking the goal...

Hato brings Saka down not far outside the Chelsea penalty area and both Odegaard and Rice are standing over it. Chelsea have just three men in the wall. Rice is going to take...

Arsenal have a corner out on the right yet Chelsea, who are the ones defending, leave four players up the pitch rather than in their own box. Is that madness or a masterstroke? The delivery from Saka goes beyond the back post, where it is then headed back across goal. Saka gets to it and then goes down but he was offside anyway.

It looked like Chelsea left four attackers upfield for that Arsenal corner. That’s one way of reducing the traffic in the six-yard box.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first five minutes of each of their three Premier League games this season. Has that ever happened before? Thanks OptaJoe:

3 - Chelsea are the first side to score in the opening five minutes of three successive Premier League games since Newcastle United in December 2024, and first ever to do so in their first three matches of a season in the competition.Blocks. pic.twitter.com/g9bum6fQkA

Fofana brings down Havertz with a rather silly challenge and Arsenal have a free-kick out on the right, with the chance to send it into the Chelsea box. Odegaard drills it low in towards the near post and picks out the run of Calafiori. The Italian’s effort is saved by Martinez’s legs and then a mad scramble for the ball ensues. It is difficult to see where the ball is and ends up going out for a goal kick. Martinez stays down and is receiving treatment to his head. It comes as a result of Gabriel’s boot flying into Martinez’s head. Should VAR be taking a look at that one? They clear it but Gabriel might count himself lucky that a review for violent conduct was not called.

Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Rogers, on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area, watches the ball onto his foot and volleys first time into the bottom left corner. A fine finish from Rogers and Chelsea have the perfect start. How will Arsenal respond?

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

The first goal Arsenal concede this season is scored by the first player they wanted to sign in the summer.

Wow. That had echoes of Eze scoring against Tottenham last season. Just as Spurs had missed out to Arsenal for Eze, Arsenal missed out to Chelsea for Rogers. So what happens? Of course, he scores. After just two minutes. I’m also pretty sure Rogers imitated the Thierry Henry celebration next to the corner flag just to rub salt into Arsenal’s wounds.

The two bosses, who have known each other since they were children, share a warm embrace before kick-off.

We are under way at the Emirates. Both sides have 100% records coming into this one but at least one of those will fall today.

Perhaps some early mind games from Arsenal as Chelsea were left waiting in the tunnel for a little while before Arsenal eventually emerged. Eventually both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has confirmed that the Ecuadorian midfielder was close but Alonso says it was not worth the risk at this stage of the season. He also confirmed that Levi Colwill being on the bench today was down to fitness.

The first game of the afternoon has just concluded at the Hill Dickinson and Everton have snatched a point at the death against Manchester United, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles scoring a screamer on his Everton debut with almost the last kick of the game to make it 2-2. It is not always particularly significant when a manager says his player can be one of the best in the world. But it is probably worth taking notice when Xabi Alonso articulates his belief that Reece James can be one of the best midfielders on the planet.

For Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Spain, Alonso was one of the finest midfielders of his generation and also played with some of the best midfielders in the world. So the Chelsea manager knows a thing or two about what it takes.

James has long been considered – when fit – one of the best right-backs in the world. But it had already been evident before the final 24 hours of the transfer window that the Chelsea player would spend a lot of time in midfield under Alonso.

Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

How chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

There’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. Chelsea only managed 25 per cent of possession against Brighton, so is this an attempt to get more of the ball? As expected, Moises Caicedo is not fit so Reece James and Romeo Lavia will need to play well.

Your Chelsea XI.#CFC | #ARSCHE pic.twitter.com/UkSmiUVgO3

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his new signing into the side.

Saturday:Newcastle 2 Bournemouth 2Brentford 1 Sunderland 1Brighton 1 Leeds 1Fulham 2 Crystal Palace 3Manchester City 1 Coventry 0Nottingham Forest 0 Tottenham 0Hull City 0 Aston Villa 0

Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

#1896. Arouca vs Rio Ave - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 26 Nov 2026 21:27, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:00

Still licking their wounds after their Taca de Portugal fourth-round exits, Arouca and Rio Ave return to action in the Portuguese Primeira Liga when they go head to head at the Estadio Municipal de Arouca on Saturday afternoon.

Rio Ave head coach Vasco Seabra will be out to haunt his former employers in his first return to the Municipal since switching teams in October after two years and 68 games in charge of the Arouquenses.

While Vitor Severino’s appointment has restored confidence in Arouca, consecutive defeats in their most recent two outings have raised fresh concerns, particularly after losing 2-1 to third-tier CD Mafra in the Taca de Portugal last Saturday.

The tie took a difficult turn for the Arouquenses when Moussa Camara and Leandro Alves put Mafra two goals up at the Estadio Municipal de Mafra, and while Ivan Barbero pulled one back in the 59th minute to spark a potential comeback, the hosts held on to see out the victory.

This followed a 1-0 defeat against Famalicao at the Estadio Municipal de Famalicao on November 6, when Paulo Moreira netted in the sixth minute of stoppage time to end Arouca’s run of three consecutive victories in the Primeira Liga.

Despite their recent slump, the Porto outfit can take pride in what had been a solid start to the campaign, as they sit fifth in the Primeira Liga standings with 20 points from 11 matches, four points behind the Champions League qualifying places.

A disciplined defence has been key to Arouca’s promising start, as they boast the joint-highest number of clean sheets in the Primeira Liga while conceding just eight goals so far - only league leaders Porto (5) have allowed fewer.

Like the home side, Rio Ave saw their Taca de Portugal journey come to an end at the hands of a lower-tier side last weekend as they fell to a 1-0 loss against Liga 3 outfit SC Vianense on Sunday.

The visitors were guilty of a toothless display in attack at the Estadio Dr. Jose de Matos, with Moises Conceicao’s 33rd-minute strike proving decisive in sending Vianense through to the cup round of 16.

This was in keeping with their struggles in the Primeira Liga, where Rio Ave are on a three-game losing streak, suffering defeats against Famalicao, Academico Viseu and Braga, while managing just four points from eight games since August 28.

Off the back of a 12th-placed finish last season, Vasco Seabra’s men have found the going considerably tougher this time around and are one of the early contenders to go down, having collected just seven points from 11 games to sit 17th in the Primeira Liga table.

With the festive period approaching, Rio Ave will head into the weekend keen to kickstart a turnaround, and they will draw encouragement from recent results against Arouca, having picked up five wins and four draws from the last 11 meetings between the two teams since August 2021.

Arouca will take to the pitch without Spanish forward Miguel Puche, who continues his lengthy spell on the sidelines since sustaining a knee injury in April’s matchup against Estrela Amadora.

Barring any late fitness issues, Puche should be the only absentee for the Arouquenses, giving Severino the luxury of a relatively full strength squad to select from this weekend.

As for Rio Ave, goalkeeper Cezary Miszta remains sidelined with a back injury, while defender Nelson Abbey is also expected to sit out the trip to the Estadio Municipal de Arouca.

Brandon Aguilera, Pedro Amaral and Ze Carlos are all listed as injury doubts, leaving head coach Vasco Seabra with a few selection decisions to make ahead of Saturday's encounter.

De Arruabarrena; Esgaio, Sanchez, Fontan, Lebedenko; Fukui, Van Ee; Trezza, Lee, Djouahra; Barbero

Van der Gouw; Tome, Mancha, Ntoi, Vrousai; Nascimento, Nikitscher; Clemmensen, Patricio, Bezerra; Blesa

Arouca have seen their form dip in recent weeks, but they back themselves against an out-of-sorts Rio Ave side,  who have lost their last four matches across all competitions.

With just nine goals scored, Rio Ave have plenty to do on Saturday against a defensively solid Arouca side, but we tip the hosts to take control of proceedings and come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1895. 54 passes completed: ‘Superb’ Liverpool colossus was ‘bossing it’ against Club Brugge

Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni was praised for a ‘superb’ performance against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The 19-year-old was restored to the Reds’ starting XI for the match at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with Alexis Mac Allister dropping to the bench as Andoni Iraola rewarded the youngster for his fine form of late.

The teenager played for 73 minutes in Belgium before he was replaced by the Argentine as the visitors sought to regain control amid a concerted spell of pressure from the home side.

Football writer Sam McGuire took to X at half-time to praise the Liverpool midfielder’s showing as he posted: ‘Trey Nyoni bossing it again. Joint most touches and he’s completed 93% of his passes.’

Elsewhere, Ian Doyle handed the youngster 8/10 in his half-time player rating for the Liverpool Echo, writing that the Reds’ number 42 ‘demonstrated superb composure in possession, especially when dealing with an increasing number of defensive situations ahead of half-time.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Handed a fourth Champions League start of the season, Nyoni repaid Iraola’s faith with a fine performance against Club Brugge tonight.

As Doyle referenced, the 19-year-old made some important defensive contributions in Belgium, dispossessing Carlos Forbs just before half-time and stopping the winger in his tracks in a dangerous position once again just after the hour mark.

Steven Gerrard proclaimed before kick-off that the teenager is ‘like a Rolls Royce’ and ‘never lets the team down’ (TNT Sports, via Sky Sports), and our number 42 underlined that reputation with an excellent showing on Wednesday, as reflected in his underlying figures from Sofascore.

It seemed harsh on Nyoni to be substituted when he was, but Iraola clearly felt that he needed more experience on the pitch with the simultaneous introduction of Mac Allister and Virgil van Dijk.

The double change was vindicated by Liverpool extending their tenuous 1-0 lead to a comfortable 3-0 margin in the final 20 minutes, but the teenage midfielder can still feel rightly proud of his performance tonight.

Mauricio Pochettino has a mountain to climb as Manchester United manager, but he may not be given the chance to do so.

Man United have conceded 10 goals in three games since his arrival, still waiting for his first victory since replacing Michael Carrick in the dugout.

Supporters will hardly have been surprised when Brentford took a 2-0 lead through Callum Wilson on Saturday, 28 November, and even less when the Bees added two more.

Many began streaming out of the stadium before full-time, and the majority are already losing belief in Pochettino's ideas and project.

United actually became the first team in Premier League history to conceded two goals in consecutive halves of football.

Fans believe that the team have finally hit rock-bottom, and then they smash through the floor with a 4-0 defeat to high-flyers Brentford.

Ultimately, the players just aren't good enough. But for the Man United owners to admit that would be admitting that they aren't good enough either.

The Glazers are hardly going to take blame, so it all falls on the manager's shoulders, even if Pochettino has only been in charge for three games.

Right now, David Moyes holds the record for the least amount of time in charge at Old Trafford in the Premier League era, lasting nine months and 22 days between July 2013 to April 2024.

Ruben Amorim is just behind the Scot, lasting one year, one month and 25 days, and they could soon be joined by Pochettino.

In fact, he could absolutely smash the record for a Man United manager's shortest-ever tenure in the Premier League era, given that his future is already in doubt.

It will be a miracle if the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss can make it to the January transfer window at this rate.

He, of course, will have incentives to drag Man United away from the relegation zone, with Keith Wyness telling Football Insider that his contract includes a "ridiculous" bonus if he does so.

However, so far, there have been very few signs that he will actually be able to manage that, and the owners may feel pressured to make a change already.

#1893. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

“We have a CLEAR long-term plan and we won’t change it because of the table.”

“We want players with the right CHARACTER — not BIG STARS. Young is better right now.”

From a fans point of view, if one big signing is the difference between scudetto and not scudetto, I would tend to disagree with Amorim.

I think his point is that it’s about making the right signings. ACM has made panic buys the last couple of years. Stick to the plan. I think Arsenal is the perfect example of this approach.

Yeah, Joao Felix and Santi GImenez were big money, so was Nkunku. But if they don’t have the right characteristics and don’t fit the squad, then they will be a net negative to the team as a whole,

It’s not good enough to say, we are 1 or 2 players away from competing, we need to go buy some random hype player. You need to buy the RIGHT players that fit the team and the existing players.

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:41

After returning to the top six of the League One table with a midweek victory, Bradford City will head to Adams Park to take on Wycombe Wanderers on Saturday.

The visitors sit sixth and within touching distance of the top two, while their hosts find themselves 15th on the back of a loss and a draw.

Wycombe Wanderers return to action at Adams Park on Saturday with the hopes of kickstarting a climb up the League One table in the midst of a disappointing run.

They spent the first five games of 2026-27 under Michael Duff, who now leads the visitors, going winless before he was replaced by Tom Hounsell who oversaw an upturn in form.

The Chairboys won three, drew one and lost one of their first five league outings under the new boss but have since put one more notch in the wins column in five further third-tier matches.

That came at home to Burton Albion alongside an FA Cup victory, before Hounsell's men lost a dramatic game to Oxford United last weekend, having led 3-0 through Jayden Wareham, Malik Mothersille and Aaron Morley and been reduced to 10 men with Dan Casey and Luke Leahy sent off before the hosts scored four goals in the final 20 minutes to snatch all three points.

Left wounded by that result, and now on the back of a midweek 1-1 draw with strugglers Bromley, Wycombe Wanderers find themselves 15th and will be keen to put another positive run together beginning with a home win at the weekend.

They meet a former boss who arrives at Adams Park in search of back-to-back victories as Bradford City manager to strengthen their standing in the playoff places.

Braford City's 2026-27 has also been a mixed one thus far, having built on their 2024-25 promotion and 2025-26 playoff loss in League One with a fast start under Graham Alexander, who departed in September, leaving them on 15 points from seven games.

Duff has since taken charge and overseen seven league matches, with the Bantams winning two, drawing four and losing one of those while keeping five clean sheets to move onto a league-high tally of 10 for the season in 15 League One matches.

Following consecutive dominant cup victories, winning 7-0 and 4-0, and a 2-2 draw against Doncaster Rovers, the Bantams headed into a second straight Yorkshire Derby on Tuesday at home to Barnsley and dished out a 3-0 beating as Stephen Humphrys scored a brace and Jake Beesley added a late third from the spot.

Now back in the top six after a blip in the early stages under Duff, while boasting the league's best defensive record and having scored 16 goals in their last four matches to begin to remedy their attacking struggles, Bradford City will bid to make it consecutive wins on Saturday to close in on the automatic promotion spots.

Wycombe Wanderers will remain without Armando Quitirna, Ewan Henderson and Danny Ings through injuries.

Dan Casey and Luke Leahy are back in contention after suspensions for their red cards against Oxford, though, and Casey should rejoin Connor Taylor at the back.

Wareham will continue to lead the line, having scored eight goals in 11 league appearances so far this season, while Caolan Boyd-Munce could again join Cauley Woodrow and Malik Mothersille in support with Fred Onyedinma having missed the last three matches.

Bradford City will field a similar starting XI from the 3-0 midweek win over Barnsley, with Bobby Pointon, Tyreik Wright and George Lapslie sidelined by injuries and key midfielder Antoni Sarcevic also set to miss out again.

They are without Ibou Touray, though, as he is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards, and he may be replaced by Corey O'Keeffe or Josh Neufville, who has returned in the last two games after an injury layoff.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod over George Pratt in midweek at the back and should again join Aden Baldwin and Matthew Pennington, while Humphrys will lead the line after Tuesday's brace and Beesley and Nick Powell will battle to come in in place of Will Swan and Adam Phillips.

The 29-year-old already has seven goals and seven assists in 17 league appearances this term, and holds the key if the Hammers are to win promotion.

Only a handful of players boast more Championship goals than the winger in 2026-27, while he leads the way for assists in England's second tier.

#1888. Angers vs Lens - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 26 Nov 2026 22:39, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 09:56

Relegation-zone Angers SCO host RC Lens in Ligue 1 on Saturday at Stade Raymond Kopa.

The home side sit 17th in the the Ligue 1 table with eight points after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Paris FC, while 11th-placed Sang et Or, on 14 points, are playing under their third head coach of the season.

Les Scoistes have won two of their 11 league games under Stephane Gilli, who replaced Alexandre Dujeux on June 9 after Dujeux resigned and moved to Lorient.

Their last six league results read lost, lost, drawn, lost, lost, lost, a stretch in which Angers have scored three goals and conceded 18.

Angers held Paris FC goalless for the first 46 minutes on Sunday, then conceded four second-half goals, two of them within 10 minutes of the restart.

Gilli returned to Stade Jean Bouin as a former Paris FC head coach, and his plan to smother their short passing worked only until Patrick Zabi opened the scoring in the 47th minute.

Amine El Ouazzani and Prosper Peter lead the club with two league goals each, but only nine have been scored in 11 games.

Angers have collected four points from six home league games, winning once and drawing once, with a 0-0 draw against Lorient on October 25 the highlight.

Gilli said after the 2-0 home defeat to Nice on November 8 that he felt he was repeating the same message after every match.

Angers have lost each of their last six Ligue 1 meetings with Lens, including a 5-1 defeat at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on March 20 in which Lanroy Machine scored their only goal.

Les Sang et Or turned to Didier Digard on November 13, three days after sacking interim head coach Yannick Cahuzac, who had replaced Dino Toppmoller on September 15.

Cahuzac lost his job six days after a 9-1 home defeat to Como in the Champions League, a result that still hangs over the squad.

Digard’s first game ended in a 1-1 home draw with Toulouse on November 21, Michael Cuisance equalising from a Florian Thauvin assist, and his first away trip brought a 3-1 defeat at RB Leipzig on Tuesday.

Lens have won four, drawn two and lost five of their 11 league games, scoring 18 and conceding 16, and they have not kept a single clean sheet.

Their 35 goals conceded in all competitions, 16 in the league and 19 in the Champions League, is the second-worst total among clubs in Europe’s five major leagues, behind Manchester United's 36.

Their away league record reads one win, one draw and three defeats, the win being a 3-1 victory at Troyes on October 17.

Lens are winless in five games in all competitions, with the last victory a 2-1 home win over Paris FC on October 24.

Thauvin, 33, has five goals and eight assists in the league, and he scored twice in Lens’ 2-1 win at Angers on November 30, 2025.

Opta data showed after Leipzig that Thauvin has lost 15 of his 17 Champions League appearances, and Lens are 33rd in the league phase with three points from five games.

On a brighter note, Lens have won their last three visits to Stade Raymond Kopa, by 2-1 in November 2022, 1-0 in August 2024 and 2-1 last season.

Gilli had only two absentees at Wednesday’s training session, goalkeeper Melvin Zinga with a shoulder problem and midfielder Bane Diatta with an ankle injury, while Joseph Kalulu was back after cutting short Tuesday’s session.

Jordan Lefort should return after a one-match suspension, and El Ouazzani is available again after missing two games, which could push Usman Simbakoli, who made his first start of the season at Paris FC, back to the bench.

For the visitors, Ruben Aguilar, hurt against Toulouse, is out alongside Odsonne Edouard, who has had adductor surgery, and Maik Nawrocki, who has a ruptured cruciate ligament.

Cuisance missed the Leipzig game through illness and remains a doubt, while Abdallah Sima, back from a thigh injury, and Ismaelo Ganiou, back from meniscus surgery, are available again.

The visitors’ away record of one win in five is a genuine concern, but a first league win since October 24 looks the most likely outcome.

#1886. “It’s beautiful” – TNT commentator was in awe of Liverpool star’s ‘delicious’ moment v Brugge

Alexander Isak is now into double digits for goals for Liverpool this season, having netted twice in the 3-0 victory away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ record signing endured a tough first campaign at Anfield after his £125m move from Newcastle, scoring just four times and being sidelined for four months due to a broken leg.

Those initial struggles now seem like a distant memory after his brace in Belgium tonight took him onto 10 goals in 16 matches for his club in 2026/27, already more than doubling his tally from the whole of last term.

Isak opened the scoring for Liverpool in the first half at the Jan Breydel Stadium and wrapped up the victory in the 83rd minute by outmuscling Brandon Mechele, advancing into the penalty area and coolly lofting the ball over Yann Sommer in the Club Brugge net.

Calling that goal for TNT Sports, Sam Matterface gushed: “That’s brilliant from Isak. He’s got away from Mechele and he’s bursting into the box, and this will seal it…oh, it’s beautiful, delicious! Such a brilliant finish.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The manner in which Isak took that clinching goal shows just how much confidence is flowing through his veins right now. Every time he gets the ball in that area of the pitch, he looks like finishing off the chance (aside from an uncharacteric miss against Manchester United on Sunday).

It isn’t just the quality of his finishing which is standing out, either – as Ian Doyle noted for the Liverpool Echo, the 27-year-old helped to create his first goal by pressing the Club Brugge defence and forcing the error from Sommer.

He also looks increasingly at ease with his fellow attackers, with a neat chemistry now forming on the pitch, and his confidence is evident in how he runs at opposition defences with an attitude of “I’ve got you!”.

John Aldridge recently claimed that Isak may well be targeting somewhere in the region of 20 to 25 goals for the season, and the Swede is already halfway to the lower end of that bracket with one more match still to play in November.

Along with fellow 2025 arrival Florian Wirtz, Liverpool’s number 9 is showing everyone why his current club spent such a vast money on him.

If he doesn’t suffer a recurrence of the injury problems which ruined his first campaign with the Reds, he could easily end up hitting or even surpassing the target that Aldridge has set.

#1884. Mainz 05 vs Union Berlin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 22:39, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 04:52

MEWA Arena will be the backdrop for a six-pointer in the lower reaches of the Bundesliga table on Saturday, when Mainz 05 host relegation-threatened Union Berlin.

Die Nullfunfer are desperate to avoid a sixth defeat on the bounce, while Die Eisernen are searching for their first win in six competitive games.

Urs Fischer rescued Mainz when he took the reins midway through last season, but his team are at risk of being dragged into a fight for their survival this time around.

Die Nullfunfer were downed 3-1 by Augsburg last Sunday, falling three goals behind before finding a way through via substitute Ransford-Yeboah Konigsdorffer.

That defeat has left Fischer's side 13th in the Bundesliga table with just 10 points from their 10 matches, a tally that has the club sitting a mere three points above 16th-placed Schalke 04 - and their 17th-placed opponents - in the relegation zone.

Mainz arrive for Saturday's clash having lost each of their past five matches across all competitions, conceding 14 goals in the process with defending that the manager described as "Slapstick."

To make matters worse, the hosts have failed to win any of their five home matches this term, losing four times and drawing once - a goalless stalemate with SC Paderborn on August 29.

Meanwhile, Mauro Lustrinelli's Union have endured a dire campaign so far and are languishing in the relegation zone, but they are far from doomed ahead of their trip to Mainz.

Die Eisernen are currently 17th with seven points, level with 16th-placed Schalke in the relegation playoff spot and within three points of Paderborn, FC Koln and Mainz, though their -18 goal-difference makes it improbable for them to climb out of the bottom three this weekend.

Lustrinelli's side were hammered 5-1 by RB Leipzig last Saturday, letting four goals in during a poor second half after heading into the break on level terms thanks to Michel Aebischer's equaliser.

That disappointment extended the Berliners' winless run to six games across all competitions, a stretch that features three defeats and three matches in which they failed to score.

Saturday's visitors have fared even worse on the road in 2026-27, losing four of their last five away games and conceding a worrisome 18 goals in those losses, not to mention their inability to find the back of the net in any of them.

Mainz will be without the versatile Dominik Kohr this weekend as he continues his recovery from an ankle injury, so expect to see Kacper Potulski, Danny da Costa and Stefan Posch start in Fischer's back three.

Elsewhere, right-sided forward Silas is closing in on return to action after spending eight months out due to a fractured tibia and fibula, though he remains a doubt for Saturday.

If the 28-year-old is unavailable, Sheraldo Becker and Phillip Tietz will start up top, supported by Ransford-Yeboah Konigsdorffer and Nadiem Amiri.

As for Union, they are missing a concerning number of defenders, including centre-backs Zeno Van Den Bosch (suspended for accumulating yellow cards), Stanley Nsoki (calf), and Felix Uduokhai (thigh), not to mention that right-back Josip Juranovic is sidelined due to illness and left-back Andrik Markgraf remains out with a knee injury.

In their absence, Marvin Friedrich and Leopold Querfeld look set to operate at the heart of the visiting backline, flanked by full-backs Christopher Trimmel and Derrick Kohn.

Further forward, wingers Livan Burcu and Robert Skov are both injured, while midfielder Rani Khedira is unavailable after feeling physical discomfort following the loss to RB Leipzig.

Thankfully for the capital club, Kastriot Imeri, Andras Schafer and Michel Aebischer should be on hand to start in the centre of the park, lining up behind Oliver Burke and Andrej Ilic.

Zentner; Potulski, Da Costa, Posch; Sano; Caci, Mwene; Konigsdorffer, Amiri; Becker, Tietz

Ronnow; Trimmel, Friedrich, Querfeld, Kohn; Kemlein; Imeri, Schafer, Aebischer; Burke, Ilic

Mainz will be desperate to avoid yet another defeat, and while that aim could be realised against their fellow strugglers, a win seems unlikely due to their dire record on home turf.

Union have been particularly poor on the road this season, and their lacklustre defending means they will realistically need to score at least once to prevent a loss.

Rangers are not currently planning to loan Vanja Dragojevic out in January despite his tough start to life at Ibrox, sources have told Football Insider.

The versatile 20-year-old midfielder was a regular for the Serbian club but has only made eight appearances for his new side since the season started.

Derek McInnes has almost completely frozen Dragojevic out in recent months, with just one substitute outing in their previous nine games.

Rangers are not currently planning to let the Serbian international leave on loan, despite his struggles, as I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast.

#1881. ‘I talked to him’ – Andoni Iraola shares injury update on Victor Munoz after Brugge ‘pain’

Andoni Iraola has shared an update on the injury sustained by Victor Munoz in Liverpool’s win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The only blemish on a terrific result for the Reds in Belgium was the sight of the Spanish winger hobbling off towards the end of the first half, appearing to hurt his knee when overstretching to try and keep the ball after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area.

A stretcher had been readied for the 23-year-old, but he was at least able to pick himself up off the ground and leave the pitch flanked by medical staff.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Iraola gave an update on Munoz’s injury, with Liverpool’s number 23 due to go for an assessment to verify the seriousness of the issue.

The Reds’ head coach said (via liverpoolfc.com): “It is the worst part of the game, definitely. He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished.

“It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock.

“In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.”

The initial signs from Munoz certainly weren’t good, with the winger on the ground for a few minutes before managing to pick himself up, but this update from Iraola at least paints a slightly better picture for now.

We still have to wait for the outcome of the assessment that he’s due to undergo today before we know how severe the injury is, and how long he’s expected to be out of action.

We can only hope that it isn’t a serious setback for the 23-year-old, who’s looked bright and effervescent in his performances for Liverpool so far and was rewarded with a rare start last night before the unfortunate body blow.

Munoz had been playing well in Brugge, too, with Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle noting how the Spaniard offered a ‘real threat with his pace and a regular outlet down the right’ until he was forced off in the 42nd minute.

Fingers crossed for good news on the winger once the medical assessment is completed.

#1880. Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth: Cherries become third club to achieve rare feat with latest Europa League win

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 22:46, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:25

Bournemouth have become just the third team to win their first five main draw matches in a major European competition.

The Cherries travelled to Vigo with a perfect record in the competition after beating Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, AC Milan and Sparta Prague.

Their impressive record looked set to end when they went a goal and a man down inside the first quarter at Balaidos.

Bournemouth showed character to recover from Bafode Diakite's red card by staging a dramatic second-half turnaround that started with Alvaro Rodriguez's equaliser.

Rayan then netted a 78th-minute winner to fire the Cherries to a 2-1 victory, sending them into an outright lead at the top of the Europa League league phase with the only 100% record out of the 36 teams.

Not only have they significantly boosted their chances of securing a top-eight finish, but the Cherries also became the third team to win their first five main draw games in European competition.

German side Nurnberg were the first team to achieve the feat on their way to reaching the quarter-finals of the 1961-1962 European Cup.

Armenian side Ararat Yerevan replicated the feat when they won the first five games of their UEFA Cup campaign in 1972-1973 before losing on penalties to Kaiserslautern in the last 16.

As well as joining Nurnberg and Ararat in an exclusive group, Bournemouth also became the first Premier League side in three years to win a competitive game after trailing at half time while being a player down.

Prior to Thursday's win, Liverpool were the last team to achieve that feat when Darwin Nunez netted a late brace in a 2-1 victory after Virgil van Dijk had been sent off in the first period.

Another SPECIAL night ❤️ ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. Sturm Graz ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Sunderland ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. AC Milan ⭕️ W 0-3 vs. Man Utd ⭕️ W 3-0 vs. Aston Villa ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Leeds ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Sparta Prague ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Ipswich ⭕️ W 2-0 vs. Nottingham Forest ⭕️ W 1-2 vs. Celta Vigo THE SPIRIT IN THIS TEAM ???

After winning 10 consecutive games in all competitions for the first time in their history, Bournemouth will now start preparation for Sunday's Premier League meeting with Fulham at Craven Cottage.

Marco Rose's side will then play two more league games against Brighton & Hove Albion and Hull City before they return to Europa League action against Viktoria Plzen on December 10.

Bournemouth head into the weekend in fifth spot in the Premier League table and just three points adrift of fourth-placed Liverpool.
